question:
Match the following states with their percentage urban population in India, as per Census 2011.

 
 

 i)
 Kerala 
 a)
 10.04%
 
 

 ii)
 Madhya Pradesh
 b)
 47.72%
 
 

 iii)
 Tamil Nadu
 c)
 27.63% 
 
 

 iv)
 Himachal Pradesh
 d)
 48.45%

options.text: i) - d, ii) - c, iii) - b, iv) - a
i) - a, ii) - d, iii) - c, iv) - b
i) - a, ii) - b, iii) - c, iv) - d
i) - b, ii) - c, iii) - d, iv) - a

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **i) Kerala - b) 47.72%**
 
• **ii) Madhya Pradesh - c) 27.63%**
 
• **iii) Tamil Nadu - d) 48.45%**
 
• **iv) Himachal Pradesh - a) 10.04%**
 
• These percentages are based on the Census 2011 data for urban population in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The urban population percentage is an important demographic indicator that helps in understanding the level of urbanization in different states.
 
• Urbanization is often associated with economic development, as cities provide more employment opportunities, better infrastructure, and improved living standards.
 
• States like Tamil Nadu and Kerala have higher urban populations, reflecting their advanced infrastructure and economic development.
 
• On the other hand, states like Himachal Pradesh have lower urban populations, which can be attributed to their geographical terrain and traditional lifestyles.
 
• This data is crucial for policy-making, urban planning, and the allocation of resources to ensure balanced regional development.
